motion: Does scientific understanding leave rational grounds for belief in God?

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins abandoned creator belief when Darwinian evolution explained biological complexity that had seemed to need a designer.
audits.rationale: The proposed span exceeds both hard limits. Events 249–258 preserve the complete personal inference in a tighter Dawkins-only span.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins found that science did not address existential questions such as purpose, death, God, and why anything exists.
audits.rationale: The Collins-only span directly identifies the questions science was not helping him answer and stays within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: After encountering theological arguments, especially C. S. Lewis's, Collins judged his objections superficial and eventually found faith more rational than atheism for him.
audits.rationale: The proposed span exceeds the character limit. Events 351–363 retain the inquiry, reassessment, two-year development, and Collins's personal qualification.

audits.recommendedProposition: Evolution powerfully explains biological diversity, but that explanatory success does not itself exclude a divine plan; it moves the proposed plan to a deeper level.
audits.rationale: The span is a complete, qualified Collins argument and meets both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: If a timeless God intended conscious creatures, evolution could be an elegant means whose outcome God knew without intervening in each step.
audits.rationale: The span supplies the intended creator, evolutionary means, timelessness, and foreknowledge bridge.

audits.recommendedProposition: Natural selection is an implausibly wasteful route for an intending creator and, because it could occur without God, makes God superfluous.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both hard limits. Events 603–616 retain both connected components of Dawkins's single method-and-redundancy objection.

audits.recommendedProposition: From a human perspective, natural selection is non-benign: competition brings starvation, predation, disease, and suffering, though Dawkins calls this a less important argument.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both hard limits and begins with garbled context. The repair preserves Dawkins's human-value qualification and his limitation of the argument's importance.

audits.recommendedProposition: Evolution's duration is not an objection from the perspective of a timeless God for whom the process is effectively instantaneous and its outcome known.
audits.rationale: This is a complete Collins-only reply to the duration objection within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins argues that a creator interested in order could choose elegant mathematical laws, whose intelligibility he regards as a signpost of intelligence.
audits.rationale: The oversized proposed span combines lawful order, fine-tuning, and divine mathematical competence. The repair supports the lawful-intelligibility claim but not the original proposition's additional inference that evolution itself was thereby rationally chosen.

audits.recommendedProposition: Because evolution builds complexity and apparent design from simplicity, adding design at the beginning betrays the bottom-up explanation that made a designer unnecessary.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 769–782 contain the complete bottom-up inference in a Dawkins-only span.

audits.recommendedProposition: Once unguided physical laws are shown capable of producing complexity and apparent design, reintroducing God undermines that explanatory argument.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and substantially duplicates m10. This later subspan isolates Dawkins's capability-to-redundancy inference, though the inventory-level overlap remains.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins accepts that evolution can generate complexity but argues that this leaves unanswered where the enabling laws of physics came from.
audits.rationale: The proposed range narrowly exceeds the character limit. Removing the introductory exchange yields a complete Collins-only concession and transition.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins says the origin of the physical constants comes close to being a good argument, unlike the moral argument.
audits.rationale: The proposed range contains irrelevant discussion and a moderator exchange and violates both limits. Events 860–864 isolate Dawkins's qualified concession.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins says small changes to the physical constants would prevent galaxies, stars, chemistry, and the prerequisites for life.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 876–889 preserve the sensitivity claim and its stated consequences.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins argues that postulating a fine-tuner merely invents away the fine-tuning problem rather than explaining it.
audits.rationale: Events 951–954 are the moderator's summary, so the proposed span wrongly attributes the explicit complexity extension to Dawkins. Events 943–950 isolate Dawkins's own explanatory objection.

audits.recommendedProposition: An infinite multiverse supplies an anthropic alternative to design, but Collins argues that its expected experimental inaccessibility also requires an evidential leap.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and includes extra setup. The repair contains the multiverse alternative, observer-selection bridge, and experimental qualification.

audits.recommendedProposition: A creator outside space and time need not have a temporal beginning, so Collins argues that the same infinite regress does not arise.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 1024–1036 retain the demand for God's creator and Collins's timelessness reply.

audits.recommendedProposition: Using God to explain why anything exists is rationally defensible and consistent with the evidence, though it is not a proof.
audits.rationale: The Collins-only span explicitly states rational defensibility and twice preserves the no-proof qualification.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins tentatively understands the multiverse as a prediction of independently reputable inflationary physics rather than an invention solely for fine-tuning.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. The repair preserves Dawkins's lack-of-expertise qualification, the anti-ad-hoc inference, and his uncertainty.

audits.recommendedProposition: Because other universes may be impossible to detect, Collins argues that choosing between multiverse and creator explanations partly depends on one's prior probability for God.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 1141–1153 retain experimental inaccessibility, the competing explanations, and dependence on priors.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins acknowledges that both speakers approach the issue with presuppositions and that his is shaped by attraction to explaining complex things through simpler ones.
audits.rationale: The span is speaker-isolated, qualified, complete, and within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Darwin's gradual explanation of complex things is elegant, whereas positing a necessarily complex God disrupts that explanatory structure.
audits.rationale: The proposed fragment begins without the positive explanatory premise and ends syntactically incomplete. The repair supplies the contrast and bridge.

audits.recommendedProposition: Theological claims that God is simple are implausible because a being capable of choosing the fundamental constants would require corresponding complexity.
audits.rationale: The Dawkins-only span directly states the divine-simplicity target and his constants-based objection within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins argues that human attempts to imagine a transcendent divine mind would be radically inadequate relative to its capabilities.
audits.rationale: The proposed span begins with the moderator and violates both hard limits. Events 1233–1241 isolate Collins's epistemic-humility reply without unrelated imagery and gender discussion.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins regards God's existence as the largest question one could ask and as a scientific question.
audits.rationale: Event 1269 crosses into the moderator. The proposed range does not supply the claimed different-universe rationale, which appears much later; the adjacent repair supports only Dawkins's classification of the question.

audits.recommendedProposition: If God exists outside nature, science may provide pieces of evidence but cannot by itself prove or disprove God's existence.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 1274–1284 retain the outside-nature premise, limitation of scientific tools, and evidence-versus-proof distinction.

audits.recommendedProposition: The universe is also interpretable as one intended to produce morally responsible, loving, beauty-appreciating creatures capable of seeking God.
audits.rationale: The span is a complete Collins-only theistic interpretation within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins challenges theistic interpretation with parasites, predators, COVID-19, hurricanes, and earthquakes.
audits.rationale: Event 1365 contains the transition into moderator speech. Events 1362–1364 isolate Dawkins's concise natural-suffering challenge.

audits.recommendedProposition: A lawful evolutionary creation can produce both beautiful and harmful outcomes, and God cannot continually intervene to prevent harms such as parasites.
audits.rationale: Event 1380 crosses into the moderator. The repaired Collins-only span preserves the lawfulness-to-nonintervention inference.

audits.recommendedProposition: Belief in miracles is inconsistent with defending suffering by saying God lets physical laws operate without interference.
audits.rationale: The Dawkins-only span directly states the alleged inconsistency and meets both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Stable natural law and miracles are consistent if divine intervention is an extreme, message-bearing exception such as the resurrection.
audits.rationale: The Collins-only span contains both the rare-message exception and the resurrection example within both limits.

audits.recommendedProposition: Selective miracles appear to betray God's stated commitment to noninterference when God declines to prevent disasters or save suffering children yet intervenes elsewhere.
audits.rationale: The span is an isolated Dawkins challenge containing the principle, contrasting cases, and inconsistency inference.

audits.recommendedProposition: An author of natural law may suspend it at pivotal revelatory moments, whereas intervention at every disaster would destroy worldly predictability.
audits.rationale: Event 1420 ends with the beginning of Dawkins's reply. Events 1410–1419 isolate Collins's revelatory-exception and predictability argument.

audits.recommendedProposition: A concentrated cluster of miracles around Jesus does not fit convincingly with God's otherwise consistent refusal to intervene in natural disasters.
audits.rationale: The span is a concise, speaker-isolated historical restatement of Dawkins's consistency objection.

audits.recommendedProposition: Dawkins concedes that standard kinship and reciprocity accounts do not directly explain several modern altruistic acts, but rejects the inference that such conduct demands a divine explanation.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 1915–1928 retain the concession, examples, targeted divine inference, and Dawkins's rejection.

audits.recommendedProposition: Kin selection and repeated interaction could install a rule to be nice to everyone, which persists after humans move beyond the small-group conditions that selected it.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and includes the separate sexual analogy. The repair isolates the ancestral mechanism, psychological rule, and persistence bridge.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins objects that describing radical altruism as a misfiring evolutionary mechanism discounts conduct humans recognize as especially noble.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and adds a lengthy independent example. Events 2003–2009 isolate Collins's evaluative objection.

audits.recommendedProposition: A natural evolutionary explanation of altruism neither dismisses nor devalues it; Dawkins can admire the conduct while explaining its origin.
audits.rationale: The Dawkins-only span explicitly distinguishes explanation from dismissal while retaining his admiration.

audits.recommendedProposition: Collins argues that cultures disagree over which actions are good or evil but share a distinction between them and a sense that people should pursue good and avoid evil.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and combines an autobiographical concession with an independently assessable moral argument. The repair isolates the latter; the concession is therefore removed from the proposition.

audits.recommendedProposition: Good and evil can describe what good and bad people do without positing a divine or independently existing moral spirit.
audits.rationale: Events 2073–2076 are Collins's reply, so the proposed range crosses speakers. Events 2066–2072 isolate Dawkins's naturalistic description.

audits.recommendedProposition: Beauty is wonderful and explanation-worthy, but analogous aesthetic preferences in peahens show that a sense of beauty can receive a natural explanation.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits. Events 2082–2096 preserve Dawkins's animal analogy, positive valuation, and natural-explanation inference.

audits.recommendedProposition: Humans have historically affirmed that they ought to do good and avoid evil; Collins finds a purely evolutionary account inadequate and treats this normativity as a possible signpost of God.
audits.rationale: The proposed span violates both limits and contains more than one extended formulation. Events 2203–2216 preserve the normative datum, evolutionary reservation, and signpost inference, while narrowing away the separate cultural-disagreement premise.

duplicates: m10 and m11 substantially duplicate Dawkins's bottom-up objection to reintroducing design after evolution explains complexity.
m39 and m42 substantially duplicate Collins's universal normativity argument; m39 is best retained only as the compact datum and m42 as the explicit signpost inference.
selectionAudit.capacityRepair: The evolution-and-design section contains five pro moves (m04, m05, m08, m09, m12), exceeding the four-per-side limit. Remove m09 from the selected inventory; its lawful-intelligibility material is partly covered by the cosmic fine-tuning sequence and its repaired span no longer supplies a distinct evolutionary argument.
selectionAudit.rationale: All major load-bearing routes are represented: epistemic scope and personal routes, evolution and explanatory redundancy, bottom-up simplicity, cosmic origins and fine-tuning, natural suffering and miracles, and morality/altruism. The separate beauty section contains only a con move, but pro appeals to beauty are present within other selected Collins moves. Only evolution-and-design violates section capacity; no other section exceeds four moves for either side.
